answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce, slashable deposit before it can submit bids, with one deposit backing only one active identity. A pulse of randomly timed challenge tasks then tests whether the agent can deliver useful work; missed or fraudulent results forfeit part of its stake. A public cipher commits each task and result for audit, while umber marks the risk reserve. Sybils remain possible, but multiplying them ties up capital and multiplies exposure to penalties, making attacks costly rather than free.
